subject.title: fix(discord): default account env fallback when accounts.default.token is blank

question: Should a blank `channels.discord.accounts.default.token` inherit top-level/env fallback for the default account, or remain an explicit opt-out like named accounts?
rationale: Both choices affect shipped Discord credential semantics, SecretRef fail-closed behavior, and setup/status output, so code review cannot safely choose the permanent compatibility rule without maintainer intent.

options.title: Align fallback across credential surfaces
options.body: Treat blank default-account token as inheriting top-level/env fallback, but update resolver, inspect/setup/doctor, SecretRef runtime assignment, and tests together before merge.

options.title: Keep blank token as opt-out
options.body: Reject this branch and instead fix the config path that injects blank default-account stubs or add a doctor repair if shipped configs need migration.

options.title: Accept runtime-only mitigation
options.body: Merge the current narrow resolver change while knowingly leaving status/setup and SecretRef behavior inconsistent until follow-up work lands.

recommendation.title: Align fallback across credential surfaces
recommendation.body: Treat blank default-account token as inheriting top-level/env fallback, but update resolver, inspect/setup/doctor, SecretRef runtime assignment, and tests together before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh authored and merged the Discord SecretRef runtime-status work that introduced the credential status behavior this PR changes.
